responses.concepts.observation: Increasing the noise causes the sensor readings to be more scattered and causes it to oscillate and give many different distance results, increasing the bias causes the truth line to move which determines how often the results were actually the correct distance away.
responses.mission_1.bias_vs_variance: Looking at the statistics it seems like the bias is normal because it goes along the average of all the points but the variance is very low since there's not a lot of differing points/readings leading to a lot of the numbers being the exact same. Bias describes how far the truth is from the data while variance describes how different the data is from each other.
responses.mission_1.more_samples: More samples may not necessarily remove tis sensor's main problem because there's just not a lot of noise or variance meaning even if more samples were added it would likely still be the same number and nothing much would change.
